About Me

A life sciences Ph.D. experienced with single-cell RNA sequencing, and spatial transcriptomics, with a strong programming skillset, who can apply deep-learning techniques to NGS data as well as integrate external omics datasets to gain biological insights. A former experimentalist who transitioned to data science, I excel at experimental design and can capably collaborate with computational and bench scientists alike. A creative and dedicated worker, who is eager to solve difficult problems, and can rapidly adapt to new circumstances. I’m seeking to make an impact on the lives of medical patients through early-stage drug discovery. This is a test

Friedrich Miescher Institute

Postdoctoral Fellow - November 2017 - December 2023

Systems neuroscientist examining the relationship between computational models of neocortical function and transcriptionally defined cell types.

  • Designed computational workflows for preprocessing, cleaning, and manipulating large-scale data sets.

Spatial Transcriptomics Project

Summary: Premenopausal women are more likely to experience more aggressive forms of breast cancer, often associated with poorer clinical outcomes compared to postmenopausal women. One potential explanation could be differences in the composition of B cell subtypes among the immune cells infiltrating the tumor. In this project, I collaborated with physicians and analyzed patient datasets to investigate the role of B cell subtypes in breast cancer samples from premenopausal and postmenopausal women.

Full report located here

Project title

Summary:Here I utilized single-cell RNA sequencing and optogenetics combined with virtual reality and FACS to discover biomarkers for computationally specific neuronal cell types. I ultimately discovered that neurons which either signal the presence of a surprising stimulus or the absence of an unexpected stimulus represent transcriptionally defined cell types with molecular markers. These experiments and analyses enabled the development of cell-type specific AAVs for labeling these populations.
